parts.label: main
parts.technique: Interpreting PMCC values on scatter diagrams (correlation)
parts.reason: S2.2 covers interpretation of scatter diagrams and informal understanding of correlation, including strength/direction language; this task only requires matching given r values to diagrams by pattern, not calculating a correlation coefficient, so the S5.1/PMCC-formula exclusion does not apply.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Justifying histogram use for continuous data
parts.reason: S2.1 covers histograms and their use for continuous data.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculating frequency density
parts.reason: Directly required for histograms under S2.1.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Linear interpolation for median and quartiles from grouped data
parts.reason: S2.3 guidance explicitly expects linear interpolation to calculate percentiles from grouped data.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Mean and standard deviation from summary statistics (Sxx)
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculation of standard deviation including from summary statistics using Sxx.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Quartile-based skewness coefficient
parts.reason: No statement mentions 'skewness' or a skewness coefficient formula; S2.3/S2.4 cover central tendency/variation and outliers but not skewness as a named concept, so this specific technique is not evidenced in the specification statements.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Alternative justification of skewness via mean/median comparison
parts.reason: This continues the skewness discussion from (e); skewness is not a named concept in any statement, so this part is also out, and it also depends on the out-of-spec part (e).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding regression line y on x using coded summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly excludes 'calculations involving regression lines'; this part requires deriving the regression line equation from Sxy/Sxx.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Converting coded regression line to original variables
parts.reason: Depends on and continues the excluded regression-line calculation from (a); regression line calculations are explicitly excluded (S2.2).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Prediction using a regression line
parts.reason: Uses the regression line from (b), which is explicitly excluded (S2.2) and the part cannot be answered without it.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Box plot construction and outlier identification
parts.reason: S2.1 covers box and whisker plots including outliers, and S2.4 covers identifying outliers using a specified rule (1.5×IQR).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Commenting on skewness of a distribution using quartile spacing
parts.reason: Skewness is not a named concept in any statement; although S2.4 allows drawing inferences from measures of variation, the specific quartile-difference skewness comparison technique is not evidenced in the spec text.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Contextual interpretation of a distribution for decision-making
parts.reason: This is a general contextual comment about the data (many delays are small) which reflects S2.4's expectation that students draw inferences/interpretations from data, and it can be answered without relying on the skewness terminology used in (b).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding constant k using sum of probabilities = 1 for discrete distribution
parts.reason: S4.1 covers discrete probability distributions; summing probabilities to 1 is basic to defining such a distribution, not a mean/variance calculation, so the S4.1 exclusion does not apply here.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculating E(X) for a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables'.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculating Var(X) for a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of variance of discrete random variables.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Variance of a linear transformation of X, Var(4-3X)
parts.reason: Depends directly on the excluded Var(X) calculation from (c); the underlying technique (variance of discrete random variable) is excluded by S4.1.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability via standardising
parts.reason: S4.2 covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability for a range
parts.reason: S4.2 covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Inverse normal calculation to find a value from a given probability
parts.reason: S4.2 covers use of the Normal distribution including solving for unknowns (questions may involve solution of simultaneous/standardising equations).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Probability from a two-way table
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers two-way tables and probability calculations.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Conditional probability from a two-way table
parts.reason: S3.2 covers conditional probability using two-way tables.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Total probability using weighted conditional probabilities
parts.reason: S3.2 covers P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B|A) and combining via tree/table reasoning to find overall probability.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Bayes'-type conditional probability using the conditional probability formula
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers the conditional probability formula P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B).
